title: Who opened a ticket
purpose: See who opened one ticket, its audit history, its form details or its complaint forms, downloaded its files, was shown its patient-marked answers or person-level key, or saw its answers or entries elsewhere, and when. Supervisors only.
summary: Each time someone opened this ticket or its form details, downloaded one of its files or was shown a patient-marked answer, newest first. For supervisors; it never shows what they saw.

tasks.title: See who opened a ticket
steps: On the ticket, open the [[More]] menu and select [[Who opened it]].
Read [[When]], [[Person]] and [[What]] for each row, newest first. Use the pager below the table for older rows.

tasks.title: Check who saw a patient-marked answer or a file
steps: Look for rows whose [[What]] is Shown a patient-marked answer or Downloaded a file. The line under it names the answer's label or the file's download name.

tasks.title: Match a row with the server's logs
steps: Give the [[Request ID]] of the row to whoever runs the deployment. The same ID is in the access log line of that request and in the change events it recorded.

good_to_know: Only supervisors (and the admin role) can open this page. Opening it, and the audit history, adds a row here too.
A row records who read what and when, never what was shown: no text, answer or file content.
Lists, searches and the dashboard that show this ticket among others are not recorded. A client organization's timeline, which shows the start of entries' text, is.
Rows are never changed or deleted. Nothing is listed from before the release that added access records.
A client portal account opening its own ticket is listed too, with Client portal in [[Capacity]].

sections.title: What is recorded
paragraphs: The application writes an access record each time a staff or client portal account opens this ticket's page, its audit history, this page, its Form details page or one of its complaint forms (Investigation decision, Findings and outcome, Review complaint: they show the complaint's rationale and findings); downloads one of its files; or is shown one of its patient-marked answers. Staff are shown such an answer only when they select Reveal, which also records a change event (kept with the form's answers, so the ticket's audit history does not list it); a client portal account is shown its own client-visible answers on its ticket page, and each such answer shown is recorded on every visit. A staff member who reveals the ticket's person-level key with Reveal key is recorded the same way (the key is never shown here).

Two other pages show part of a ticket and are recorded for it: a client organization's timeline, once for each ticket whose entries a page of it shows (it shows the start of each entry's text), and a client's new ticket started with Request again from this ticket, which copies some of the client's own answers (never patient information) into the new form.

A ticket page drawn again after a refused reply, note or contact is recorded as opened again. A page that is refused (Not found, or not permitted), a reveal sent to Confirm it is you first, a page that failed with a server error, a page answered in place of the one drawn (for example when the session was signed out in another tab while it was drawn) and a HEAD request, which answers without the page, record nothing. If the record cannot be written, the page is not shown: the request fails with a server error instead.
Not recorded: lists, searches, the dashboard, and the action pages that show only the ticket's number, such as Assign, Status and Edit category and priority. The search text is never recorded.

items.label: When
items.description: The date and time to the second, in the laboratory's time zone, by the database's clock when the record was written, just after the page was drawn.

items.label: Person
items.description: The account's name, with its username below, as they stand now. A record keeps the account, not its name. An account that no longer exists shows its number.

items.label: Capacity
items.description: Laboratory staff for a staff account, Client portal for a client portal account. An account's kind never changes.

items.label: What
items.description: Opened the ticket, Opened the audit history, Opened who opened it, Opened the form details, Opened a complaint form, Downloaded a file, Shown a patient-marked answer, Shown a person-level key, Shown on the organization's timeline, or Answers copied with Request again. For a file, the line below gives its download name (the ticket number and the file's number, never the name it was uploaded with); for an answer, the label of its form field; for a person-level key, the link's number, never the key or its masked form.

items.label: Request ID
items.description: The identifier the server gave the request that read it, also sent to the browser in the X-Request-ID header and written in the server's access log. Change events made from this release on carry the same identifier. Not recorded for a row written without one.

items.label: Access records
items.description: The panel's title. The number beside it counts the rows for this ticket recorded when you opened the page. Twenty-five rows per page, newest first; the pager below the table moves through older rows, as they stood when you opened the first page, so a row recorded since (your own visit included) never moves another to the next page. Open the page again from the ticket to see newer rows.

items.label: Nothing recorded yet
items.description: Shown when nobody has opened the ticket since the release that added access records.

items.label: Back to the ticket
items.description: The link above the panel returns to the ticket page, keeping the list you came from. The link in the panel's footer opens the audit history.

sections.title: Who can use this page
paragraphs: Supervisors and the admin role, for any ticket they may read. Other staff are refused. A ticket in a restricted category that you may not read answers Not found. Client portal accounts cannot open it. Your account and the records are read together, at one moment, when the page opens.
The page is read-only. Access records are kept apart from the audit history, which lists changes, and the database refuses to change or delete them. They have no retention period in the application.
